subject: capacity.training
name: Leadership Excellence in Africa's Public Sector (LEAPS) programme
position_end: Running, implemented by the African Capacity Building Foundation with Gates Foundation support and aimed at leadership and governance capacity for public financial management reform; the foundation's position is that reform in Africa stalls on leadership gaps, institutional fragmentation and resistance to change rather than on policy

subject: include.divides
name: Women and girls digital-inclusion accelerator
position_end: An industry-body accelerator backed by two private foundations opened its next call for digital-inclusion solutions for women and girls across India and sub-Saharan Africa, with a grant amount listed at INR 42,000,000

subject: geopol.china
name: ATU memorandum with the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
position_end: A memorandum signed in 2025 between the African Telecommunications Union and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology on joint research, capacity development, technology transfer and next-generation networks, which the Union names as the foundation for its Secretary-General's participation in an Advanced Seminar on African Digital Development and Transformation that opened in Hangzhou on 24 August 2026, where he carried the priorities of its 52 member states

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese artificial-intelligence cooperation centres with the African Union
status: Implemented, one centre of the announced programme
position_end: The China-Africa Digital Technology Cooperation Center was formally inaugurated at Hangzhou on 28 August 2026 as a standing operational platform for results display, market-entry services, industry matchmaking, training and development research, four days after running its first high-level training programme; the opening drew officials, think tanks and executives from 18 African countries and the African Telecommunications Union, UNDP, UNICEF and the Smart Africa Alliance, and a same-day matchmaking session produced cooperation intentions in digital infrastructure, AI applications, cybersecurity and digital-skills training

subject: tech.innovate
name: Multi-country mapping of innovation-support organisations
position_end: A EUR120,000 procurement opened by a European development agency for a multi-country mapping of African entrepreneurship- and innovation-support organisations under a Europe-Africa digital innovation programme

subject: finance.new
name: Africa Finance Corporation digital bond
position_end: CHF 350m raised on a five-year digital bond listed, traded and settled on a regulated digital exchange — stated as the first by an African institution — priced at a 1.4925% coupon and arranged by two European banks; it is the issuer’s fourth and largest Swiss franc issuance

subject: finance.new
name: Africa50 Infrastructure Acceleration Fund
position_end: Fourth close of about US$330m, joined by British International Investment's US$20m commitment alongside the African Development Bank, the International Finance Corporation and more than 20 African institutional investors; the fund, managed by Africa Infrastructure Investment Partners, directs capital to logistics, power, water and sanitation and social infrastructure as well as digital connectivity; the size and date of earlier closes are not established

subject: finance.new
name: African share of a European development group's digital portfolio
position_end: EUR 558m, 59% of the group's standing digital portfolio of about EUR 948m and its largest region by a wide margin, against EUR 293m newly committed group-wide across 47 projects in 2025 and 152 projects in execution in 57 countries and territories (2025, published 2026-08-28)

subject: finance.new
name: BIASHARA 2063 project (AU Commission institutional systems)
position_end: A World Bank-financed programme building the Commission's own institutions and systems, procuring wireless infrastructure for its headquarters; no envelope, timetable or results framework held

subject: finance.new
name: Capital raised by startups from a technology company's African accelerators
position_end: More than US$1bn raised cumulatively since 2017, with a stated survival rate above 90% against a 70-80% failure rate for the wider ecosystem (2026-08)

subject: finance.new
name: Development-finance and infrastructure-fund partnership
position_end: A British development finance institution and a continental infrastructure fund announced a strengthened partnership to scale infrastructure financing across Africa, connectivity among the named sectors; no commitment amount, fund vehicle, country allocation or timetable is published

subject: finance.new
name: Growth-capital investment in a pan-African messaging infrastructure provider
position_end: US$12m into a provider of application-to-person messaging — one-time passwords, transaction alerts and delivery updates — operating across 35 African countries through 15 operator partnerships

subject: finance.new
name: KOICA Youth Leadership Programme
position_end: US$34m stated by Korea for a programme coupling public governance and policy development with artificial-intelligence-driven digital government, hosted by the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration for 200 participants from Ghana, Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal and Cameroon, in three phases - online training, in-country sessions, and a funded 14-day study visit to Korea for the best performers

subject: finance.new
name: Limited-partner commitments to African private-capital funds
position_end: 64 commitments in the second quarter of 2026 against 53 a year earlier, with disclosed value of US$272m against US$847m in the same quarter of 2025 and US$1.18bn in the first quarter of 2026; no disclosed commitment above US$50m, and information technology appeared in 61% of commitments against 17% a year earlier

subject: finance.new
name: LINGUA Africa language-model grants
position_end: 26 projects covering more than 50 African languages, dialects and sign languages across 47 countries, each awardee eligible for up to US$250,000 in cash and US$400,000 in compute credits; health, agriculture and justice are the stated use cases

subject: finance.new
name: Stage mix of a development financier's African portfolio
position_end: 79% of one development financier's African deals are at Series B or later, so it operates less like a venture fund than a later-stage investor

subject: gov.regional
name: Africa Internet Governance Forum
position_end: The fifteenth annual forum is scheduled for the Labadi Beach Hotel, Accra, from 2 to 5 November 2026, running a main forum alongside youth, parliamentarian and Day Zero tracks and the African School on Internet Governance; session times, venues and speakers were not published when the schedule was read

subject: gov.regional
name: African Financial Stability Committee
position_end: Hosted by the Association of African Central Banks and running a Macroprudential Policy Development and Implementation Working Group and an African Financial Stability Report Working Group; the continental portal carrying its mandate, structure, member central banks, meeting calendar and working groups was built and launched by the Central Bank of Egypt rather than by the association's secretariat, executing a decision of the 47th Assembly of Governors of 2025-11-28

subject: gov.regional
name: African Financial Stability Report
position_end: Inaugural 2024-2025 edition endorsed for publication by the Association of African Central Banks' 47th Assembly of Governors at Yaounde on 2025-11-28 and released in July 2026, covering 46 countries on data as at December 2024 with analysis through 2025. Its payments chapter, built from 26 central banks' published data, records that about 67 per cent of the continent's payment infrastructures are national systems run by central banks and 56 per cent of established systems handle retail, and finds the landscape fragmented, interoperability still limited and the operationalisation of regional and pan-African systems facing continuing challenges

subject: gov.regional
name: African Union Archives and Repository Project
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: A project to establish an African Union archives and repository, dormant and now under reinstatement: the AU Commission received a South African delegation at headquarters in Addis Ababa on 7 September 2026 for an introductory meeting at the Cabinet of the Chairperson, reviewing background and current status and setting out the issues for a working visit. No scope, budget, timetable or hosting arrangement is published.

subject: gov.regional
name: Association of Regulators of Information and Communications for Eastern and Southern Africa (ARICEA)
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: A COMESA-linked association of communications regulators across Eastern and Southern Africa, holding its 14th annual general meeting in Livingstone, Zambia, on 9 September 2026, at which COMESA's assistant secretary-general for programmes called for stronger, more predictable and more agile regulatory frameworks to match digital expansion across the region. Membership, mandate and any harmonisation instrument the association issues are not published in this account.

subject: gov.regional
name: ATU Strategic Plan 2027-2031
position_end: A draft Strategic Plan for 2027-2031 was circulated to member states for comment ahead of CPL-26; the draft is not published, and no adopted plan, budget or final acts of the conference are held

subject: gov.regional
name: State parties to the AfCFTA
position_end: 49 of 54 signatories had deposited instruments of ratification as at July 2026, and Somalia is to become the 50th state party on depositing its instrument in September 2026, having agreed with the Secretariat a sequence running from ratification through domesticating the electronic tariff book and configuring preferential tariffs in its customs administration to a first shipment (2026-08)

subject: gov.policy
name: Africa Technology Policy Tracker
position_end: A continental register built by the Carnegie Endowment with the African Telecommunications Union, consolidating national digital-economy laws, policies and regulations across infrastructure, platforms, skills and innovation; it indexes adopted documents only, weights nothing and assesses neither implementation nor rights compatibility. The counts reported on 2026-07-30 are 60 documents for Nigeria, 59 for Rwanda and 19 for Zambia

subject: gov.protect
name: African Union Data Policy Framework
position_end: In force as the continental reference framework, with about a third of the 54 member states aligned to it on a 2026-08-11 analysis, and 25 national regulatory sandboxes recorded across 15 countries by late 2024; no compliance mechanism, reporting cycle or enforcement route is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial-intelligence startups counted in a continental census
position_start: Not held: the deposit's 2022 and 2025 editions are not held, so the base carries no count before this one
position_end: 224 firms across 22 countries and a Pan-African category, founded 2002 to 2025; 195 active and 18 defunct by operating status, and 143 early stage, 72 growth stage and 9 mature by stage

subject: tech.ai
name: Common African Position on AI and its Impact on Peace, Security, Democracy and Development
position_end: The Council requested the Commission to expedite the comprehensive study and the Common African Position and submit them for its consideration; a Policy Brief on AI for Peace, Security and Governance in Africa is reported in progress and no text is published

subject: gov.standards
name: Continental ICT standardisation alignment
position_end: Talks opened on a coordinated continental approach across the standards lifecycle, from development through harmonised adoption and implementation by countries, naming fragmentation and the failure to translate continental and international standards into national frameworks as the problem

subject: gov.protect
name: Network of African Data Protection Authorities (NADPA-RAPDP)
position_end: The Fifth Board - Cabo Verde, Cote d'Ivoire and Zimbabwe - signed a declaration on 3 September 2026 proclaiming 21 September as Africa Data Protection Day, executing a decision of the network's ninth annual general meeting in May 2026; no membership count, secretariat budget or work programme is held (2026-09)

subject: tech.ai
name: Public capital committed to the AU Continental AI Strategy
position_end: About US$150m of public capital committed by African governments against an implementation cost the Strategy itself prices at between US$250bn and US$500bn - a fraction of one per cent - and an ambition to add US$1.5 trillion to Africa's GDP by 2030; independent research over the Strategy's first eighteen months found the funding heavily concentrated in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Egypt, with little reaching the remaining member states

subject: tech.ai
name: Training data for African languages
position_end: A research company has set out to build training data for a thousand African languages, after years in which the scarcity of that data was what stopped anyone building language technology for the continent (2026-09)

subject: dpi.id
name: Adults holding official identification in Sub-Saharan Africa
position_end: 81% of adults, 82% of men against 79% of women, a 3.56-point gender gap (2025)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: AfCFTA Customs Modernisation Project
position_end: A public-private partnership under which Bergmans Security Consultants and Supplies Limited mobilises the financing for customs digital solutions, secure electronic exchange of customs information, coordinated border management, One Stop Border Posts, transit systems, electronic cargo tracking, non-intrusive inspection technology, integrated data centres, multilingual customs portals, risk management and data analytics across participating State Parties; the agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding concluded in July 2026 and nothing is recorded as deployed; a US$3.1bn contract was signed with a Nigerian security consultancy to digitise customs across the 50 member states, aiming at real-time cargo tracking and reduced revenue leakage

subject: infra.connect
name: Africa Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Report
position_end: Phase 1, Country Pilots, put out as an open consultancy tender at a stated budget of US$165,000, funded jointly by the African Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance; the pilot countries and the terms of reference are not established

subject: dpi.mis
name: African Regional Integration Synthesized Index (ASRII) platform
position_end: The African Union Commission's platform for submission, validation, automated computation and dissemination of regional integration scores across political, economic, infrastructure, and human and social pillars, developed with the regional economic communities, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Development Bank to replace manual data collection. Deployment to the regional economic communities began with a four-day training of 20 core participants at the ECOWAS Commission in Abuja on 4-7 August 2026, at which its Secretary General said the Commission holds no centralised database of the status, amendments and implications of regional legal protocols

subject: infra.store
name: African share of global data-centre capacity
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: Put at 0.6% of world data-centre capacity by the chief executive of a pan-African fibre operator, speaking on the sidelines of ITW Africa 2026 in Nairobi on 10 September 2026, who named it the concern African telecom executives raise most, with cross-border connectivity the only issue close to it.

subject: dpi.pay
name: African take-up of China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System
position_end: a cross-border payments startup launching direct yuan payouts into Chinese bank accounts from dollar, euro, sterling and stablecoin balances, alongside continental take-up of China's own cross-border interbank system

subject: infra.connect
name: Airtel Africa network expansion programme
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: US$1.1 billion earmarked by the operator for expansion and upgrade of its network across 14 African markets, its chief executive said in a broadcast interview reported 10 September 2026, with annual spending stated to have risen from about US$120 million to about US$390 million and Nigeria named its largest market.

subject: infra.store
name: Amazon Web Services investment in African cloud infrastructure
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: More than US$819 million stated as invested in African infrastructure since 2018 and a further US$1.5 billion committed to 2029, with 154 services available in the Cape Town cloud region; the company's general manager for Sub-Saharan Africa told a Johannesburg summit on 10 September 2026 that its Africa strategy is increasingly aimed at local developers building for regional markets, and claimed more than one million Africans trained in cloud and AI skills.

subject: dpi.id
name: APAI-CRVS (Africa Programme on Accelerated Improvement of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)
position_end: The 2017-2026 decade is closing and a 2027-2036 phase is opening; the African eCRVS Shared Asset (ACSA) is named as the shared continental standard intended to cut fragmented digital procurement across country systems, and Equatorial Guinea's Justice Ministry timed a free registration campaign for children aged 0-5 (10-14 August 2026) to the decade's close. No AU statement of the new phase's content, financing or targets is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: COMESA digital retail payments platform
position_end: The regional clearing house published the scheme rulebook setting operational and governance rules for instant low-cost cross-border retail payments, and a gender audit and strategy to 2030 drawn from research along the Malawi-Zambia corridor; it advertised three platform posts on 24 August 2026 - head of technology, platform and infrastructure engineer and security engineer - whose duties establish that the platform is built on Mojaloop, runs an AWS production environment against an on-premises staging footprint and Kubernetes clusters, and that the engineering, infrastructure and information-security functions are being recruited rather than staffed

subject: infra.connect
name: Commercial 5G deployment and adoption across the continent
position_end: 61 operators across 37 African markets had launched commercial 5G services by the end of May 2026, 40 of them also running 5G fixed wireless access, after first launches in Algeria, Comoros, Egypt, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia over the preceding twelve months; 5G connections in Africa are put at just under 100 million by the end of 2026, 6.2% of total mobile connections, against a projected 3.4 billion and 37% worldwide, and among sixteen focus countries only Mauritius and South Africa had 5G population coverage above 50% as of May 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: Commercial stablecoin payout rail across African markets
position_end: A stablecoin payments platform partnered a local payout provider to widen stablecoin payouts across African markets, letting businesses settle into local currency through the partner’s rails (2026-09)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Continental data governance frameworks
position_end: Three drafts - data categorisation and data sharing, cross-border data flows, and a continental open data strategy - validated with member states and regional economic communities; none submitted to AU policy organs and none published

subject: infra.store
name: Continental dependence on foreign public cloud
position_end: African artificial-intelligence startups are exposed to hidden financial and operational risk where a large share of workloads sits with a single provider, against which a new generation of African-founded sovereign and low-latency cloud providers is emerging

subject: dpi.id
name: Continental ID and data-protection law analyser
position_end: An open-source tool launched by a university research network comparing identity and data-protection laws across more than 50 African countries, built as a retrieval-augmented chatbot and stated as intended to help states harmonise their frameworks; no usage figure, governance arrangement or maintenance commitment is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cost of sending money within Africa
position_end: Put at 8.78% of the amount sent against the SDG target of 3% (2026-08)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cost of sending US$200 to Sub-Saharan Africa
position_end: Put at 8.46% of the amount sent in the third quarter of 2025 against a global average of 6.36% and the United Nations target of 3%, with banks the costliest channel at close to 15% on average, much of it carried in exchange-rate spreads rather than disclosed fees (2025-Q3)

subject: infra.store
name: Data centres the AfCFTA Secretariat states digital trade requires
position_end: More than 700, against about 220 on the continent, on the Secretary General's statement at Marrakech
sources: 2026-04-08 Africa's digital trade push requires 700 data centres, says AfCFTA chief

subject: infra.connect
name: IPv6 capability across the AFRINIC service region
position_end: Put at 6% against a world average of 44%, with only eight African countries above 20%, fifteen between 10% and 19% and fifteen below 1%; three million IPv4 addresses have been recovered under the soft-landing policy since 2020 without a proven rise in IPv6 deployment (2026-06)

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile internet users and their measured economic value
position_end: 416 million Africans used mobile internet in 2025, generating a measured US$240bn of economic value, put at 7.8% of continental GDP

subject: dpi.registry
name: OHADA Uniform Act on General Commercial Law (AUDCG) and the RCCM business register
position_end: The founding instrument for the business register across OHADA's seventeen member states: it creates and governs the Registre du Commerce et du Credit Mobilier, defines the merchant and entreprenant statuses, sets the register's organisation and registration rules and the national and regional company-record files, and provides for their computerisation

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment Systems Directive for Africa (PSDA)
position_end: Directed to be led by central banks rather than an external entity, with the Assembly's own task force on payment system integration to lead harmonisation; no draft directive held

subject: dpi.id
name: Smart Africa digital identity blueprint
position_end: The alliance secretariat's first-edition blueprint for mutually recognised digital identity across member states, setting out the trust alliance, levels of assurance and the case for interoperable identity, drawn up after a member-state workshop

subject: dpi.pay
name: Stablecoin settlement rails serving African cross-border payments
position_end: Described by a pan-African payments operator's product chief as moving from speculative use into the plumbing of remittances and business settlement, on the evidence of Mastercard's agreement to acquire BVNK at up to US$1.8bn and Visa's stablecoin-card expansion through Stripe's Bridge into more than 100 countries, African markets among them; a first named African deployment is Flutterwave's tie-up with Caliza offering USD accounts with USDC and USDT conversion. At a UN Economic Commission for Africa webinar on 18 August 2026, market supervisors from Uganda's Capital Markets Authority, the Bank of Ghana and the Financial Services Commission of Mauritius set out three national approaches to virtual assets and stablecoins and agreed on consumer protection, financial stability, regulatory clarity and monetary sovereignty as shared objectives, arguing that compatible outcomes and supervisory cooperation matter more than identical legislation; the Commission put continental digital-asset users above 54 million, Nigeria alone at about 25.9 million, against a global tokenised money market that passed US$300bn in 2025. On 5 September 2026 the chief executive of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System disclosed that the system is exploring ways to support stablecoins and other digital currencies within its payments ecosystem, naming the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Securities and Exchange Commission as regulators whose approach he endorsed, and said announcements could follow

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Standing in the global cybersecurity index
position_end: Mauritius, Rwanda, Kenya, Tanzania and Ghana in the top tier; Benin, Togo, Zambia and South Africa in the second; the majority of the continent below, scored across legal, technical and organisational measures, capacity building and international cooperation

subject: infra.store
name: Time for a data centre to reach 85% occupancy
position_end: Six to eight years in African markets against two to three in Europe, on the Africa Data Centres Association's 2026 Economic Report, which also puts 80-90% of the continent's data as still processed and stored abroad and projects the market at US$9.2bn by 2029

subject: dpi.pay
name: Unmet trade finance demand
position_end: US$74bn to US$100bn of unmet trade finance demand, with commercial banks intermediating about 23% of the continent's trade against 40% over 2011 to 2019, and intra-African trade at US$213.8bn in 2025 (2026-08)

subject: capacity.training
name: African Institute of Informatics (IAI-Cameroun)
position_end: Operating as an inter-state training institution, with the regional commission opening collaboration on education and digital skills (2026-08)

subject: include.access
name: Economic inclusion of refugees in Central Africa
position_end: Diagnosed under the regional inclusive and resilient value chains project, following a private-sector-for-refugees framework (2024)

subject: gov.regional
name: Cameroon-Chad digital cooperation agreement
position_end: Concluded between the two communications ministries as a bilateral step inside the region's digital integration (2025-05)

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional harmonisation of remittance policies (ECCAS)
position_end: Country diagnostics on remittance policy and its regional harmonisation, on data through November 2023 (2025-04)
sources: 2025-04-01 Regional Harmonization of Remittance Policies in ECCAS - Burundi

subject: gov.protect
name: CEMAC Regulation 01/20 on protection of banking consumers
position_end: Community consumer-protection rules for users of banking, microfinance and payment services across the six member states: fair treatment, information and transparency duties, contractual balance, data-protection duties, complaint-handling and mediation

subject: dpi.pay
name: CEMAC Regulation 04/18 on payment services
position_end: Regulation 04/18 remains in force and a draft 2026 replacement is under consideration, envisaged to enter into force on 1 January 2027: mandatory strong authentication, a reversed burden of proof on fraud disputes, a protected fund-safeguarding account for payment institutions, market opening to fintechs and aggregators, and a twelve-month regulatory sandbox

subject: infra.connect
name: Central African Republic interconnection through South Sudan
position_end: Announced to reduce dependence on fragile regional networks and improve access to international capacity (2026-05)

subject: dpi.pay
name: GIMACPAY interoperability platform
position_end: The community's converged card, mobile and money-transfer interoperability platform, operated across the six member states by the regional interbank grouping and carrying 79 participants on the operator's own description

subject: data.statistics
name: ICT benchmarking across Central Africa
position_end: Funded to benchmark ICTs across the zone's telecommunications regulators and national statistics offices (2021)

subject: infra.connect
name: Nigeria-Equatorial Guinea subsea cable
position_end: Signed to expand broadband capacity and regional cybersecurity between West and Central Africa (2026-02)
sources: 2026-02-24 Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea subsea cable strengthens connectivity

subject: dpi.registry
name: Regional support for birth registration
position_end: The Francophonie organisation restated continuing support for advancing birth registration across Central Africa (2025-08)
sources: 2025-08-12 La Francophonie supports birth registration efforts across Central Africa, Madagascar

subject: include.divides
name: Regional digital access gap
position_end: Both regional bodies state that gaps in internet access, digital awareness and technological inclusion continue to threaten a connected regional market (2026-05)

subject: finance.new
name: East Africa data-centre and connectivity financing (EIB/AXIAN, RMB/Wingu Africa)
position_end: Rand Merchant Bank backed a Wingu Africa data-centre expansion across Ethiopia, Djibouti and Tanzania; the European Investment Bank granted AXIAN Telecom financing for 4G/5G rollout reaching Tanzania (and Madagascar); AXIAN separately pledged 4G expansion investment under the Partner2Connect initiative reaching Tanzania (and Comoros and Madagascar). Deal values and completion dates for the XEA-relevant legs specifically are not broken out in the reports held

subject: gov.regional
name: EAC Protocol on Regional Digital Integration
position_end: Before partner-state legislatures: Burundi's communications minister told senators in January 2025 that adopting the protocol is crucial to the country's ICT infrastructure (2025-01)

subject: gov.regional
name: Harmonisation of cybersecurity legal frameworks
position_end: A commissioned comparative study and recommendations to harmonise cybersecurity, cybercrime, data protection, digital identity, e-commerce and digital-authentication law across member states

subject: tech.ai
name: East African AI Policy Outlook Report (CIPIT)
position_end: CIPIT's four-country baseline, deliberately without a ranking, splits its sample two ways: Kenya and Rwanda have adopted national AI instruments and are building coordination around them, while Tanzania and Uganda are still developing strategies off existing digital and data-protection frameworks

subject: tech.ai
name: Regional higher-education quality assurance under AI
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: The 15th annual East African higher education quality assurance forum met in Kigali on 7 September 2026, bringing together higher education regulators and institutions from across the region to consider whether today's degrees prepare graduates for tomorrow's labour market; the host country's education minister told it the region must rethink how it defines and assures quality as artificial intelligence changes how knowledge is produced, taught and applied.

subject: gov.protect
name: Surveillance and spyware use against civil society (East and Southern Africa)
position_end: Civil-society organisation Unwanted Witness documented a pattern of surveillance threats — including spyware — used against civil society across East and Southern Africa; no government response or independently verified incident count is held

subject: data.statistics
name: EACO Regional Communications Sector Statistics Report
position_end: EACO's first regulator-submitted dataset covering all seven member states records 334.69 million active mobile subscriptions in 2025 and mobile money value up 19.6% across the five reporting countries; DRC and South Sudan reported no transaction values at all, and every mobile-money figure is presented in US dollars though EACO's own stated methodology is local currency, with no exchange rate, conversion date or basis given

subject: infra.store
name: East African data-centre market
position_end: Assessed in a regional market brief prepared for donor and investment-facility partners (2025-05)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: GovTech Maturity Index 2025 — East African benchmarking (World Bank)
position_end: The World Bank's 2025 GovTech Maturity Index placed Tanzania in Group A ('Extensive') alongside Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and Egypt, the index now weighting interoperability and adoption over launched portals — working as peer pressure across East Africa's digital states
sources: 2026-01-26 Tanzania's GovTech success raises bar for East Africa's digital states

subject: infra.cybersec
name: IGAD regional cybersecurity exercise
position_end: Run across the bloc, with one national computer emergency response team singled out for its performance (2026-07)

subject: dpi.mis
name: IMPULSE study — newborn-data electronic health information systems
position_end: The IMPULSE study examined the functionalities of electronic routine health information systems related to newborn data across Uganda, Ethiopia, Tanzania and the Central African Republic; findings are the study's own and no follow-up policy response is on file

subject: dpi.id
name: Mutual recognition of national identity documents
position_end: A 2018 study for the regional bloc set out a four-milestone architecture for regional identity interoperability, recording that South Sudan had issued more than a million identity cards by then (2018-08)

subject: gov.regional
name: AI Forward Summit 2026
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: A regional artificial-intelligence summit opened at Yasmine Hammamet, Tunisia, on 9 September 2026, organised by the Arab information and communication technologies organisation with Tunisia's communication technologies ministry under the theme 'Shaping the future of AI: from vision to value'. A secretary of state told the opening that the summit has become an important forum for dialogue on the future of AI in Arab countries and on making the technological revolution a lever for development, cooperation and peace; the Arab League secretary-general's participation was presented as a commitment to joint Arab action.

subject: infra.connect
name: Algerian 5G rollout
position_end: Launched on USD 492 million of licences awarded to the three mobile operators (2025-12)

subject: capacity.research
name: Research and development spending against the regional target
position_end: No member state has reached the regional target of 1% of GDP, or the continental target of 1.5% (2026-08)

subject: finance.new
name: UK science and technology accelerator programme
position_end: A three-year programme of up to GBP2.5m out to expressions of interest, covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and digital access and inclusion alongside climate, energy, health and space, with a primary focus on South Africa and a first-year focus on Zimbabwe and Zambia

subject: gov.regional
name: CRASA (Communications Regulators Association of Southern Africa)
position_end: The association opened its 2026/27 financial year with the first meeting of its Finance, Risk and Audit Committee, a two-day hybrid session in Maseru on 20 and 21 August 2026 hosted by the Lesotho Communications Authority, at which the committee and the secretariat reviewed financial and audit matters and assessed institutional risk across the association's regional programmes. No budget, audit opinion, risk register or programme list reaches the base from it. Its consumer and stakeholder policy committee held the financial year's first ordinary in-person meeting at Gaborone from 2 to 4 September 2026 to advance the 2026/27 workplan (2026-09)

subject: gov.regional
name: Promotion of regional capital-market integration
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: The regional secretariat and the committee of member-state stock exchanges took part in an investment congress in Dubai from 7 to 9 September 2026, promoting the region as an integrated investment destination and regional capital-market integration as a catalyst for investment and industrialisation; the congress brings together governments, businesses, institutional investors, sovereign wealth funds and development finance institutions.

subject: gov.regional
name: Southern African Development Community (SADC)
position_end: Chaired by South Africa from the 46th Ordinary Summit at Durban on 17 August 2026, taking over from Zimbabwe, with digital security named among the incoming chair's strategic priorities alongside energy, water, industrialisation and regional infrastructure, and accelerated implementation of SADC Vision 2050 and the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan stated as the frame

subject: tech.ai
name: SADC Regional Artificial Intelligence Strategy and Regulatory Framework
status: In development, reported by a member state rather than by the Secretariat
position_end: Under development according to Malawi's ICT ministry (2026-06); no draft, adoption date or Secretariat document held; a regional workshop at Harare on data governance in the artificial-intelligence age, convened with the World Bank, a continental alliance and a United Nations agency, set out to harmonise member states' data policy for readiness

subject: dpi.exchange
name: One-stop border posts and digitised border systems
position_end: A chairship priority tying one-stop border posts to the corridor trip monitoring system that integrates transport, immigration and customs data, to online permitting and operator accreditation, to one member's electronic visa and travel authorisation, and to a proposed regional tourism visa, with progress to be measured in border-crossing times reduced rather than agreements signed

subject: infra.connect
name: Regional connectivity indicators
position_end: Internet penetration 57.2%, 4G population coverage 79.2% and mobile penetration 95.2%, the last already past the regional target set for 2030 (2026-08)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SADC Agricultural Information Management System
position_end: Member-state readiness under assessment with the FAO and the EU; no platform, membership or timetable held

subject: infra.connect
name: SADC shared satellite
position_end: A technical submission on orbital positions filed with the ITU and the radiocommunication sector met to secure the slot, with a working group created to assess financing mechanisms and payment model; the project is stated to be at an early stage and no cost, launch date or operator is held (2026-08)

subject: capacity.training
name: AGRHYMET-ENABEL land-degradation monitoring capacity programme
position_end: A regional project run by the AGRHYMET regional centre with Belgian development funding across Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Senegal has trained 236 specialists in satellite-image interpretation and land-cover mapping, the Trends.Earth tool for assessing land degradation, the EX-ACT tool for soil and vegetation carbon estimation, and mobile data collection on KoboToolbox; the countries report better harmonisation of monitoring tools and methods, and the carbon accounting it enabled found the land-use sector substantially under-estimated in earlier nationally determined contributions

subject: capacity.training
name: BCEAO/COFEB certifying programme in digital finance
position_end: In its fourth edition, run by the monetary union's central bank training centre with Luxembourg's House of Training-ATTF: four modules over about nine months and 84 hours, aimed at senior staff of credit institutions, e-money issuers and microfinance institutions, one candidate per institution, participation fees of FCFA 1.2m, an 80% pass mark per module and a final project defended before a jury at Dakar

subject: capacity.training
name: EU-ECOWAS EPSG support for fact-checking platforms
position_end: Two Nigerian organisations selected for in-kind technical support covering digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and verification systems, with training in AI, digital investigations and deepfake detection, and admission to a regional cross-border verification network; no amount, duration or start date is stated

subject: geopol.china
name: China-aid ECOWAS Headquarters Building
position_end: Handed over to the Commission, the second international-organisation office complex China has built in Africa; China describes cooperation extending into the digital economy and names no digital programme, figure or instrument, and the Commission's own release names no digital component

subject: tech.innovate
name: ECOWAS Startup Awards
position_end: A second edition launched by the Commission's private sector and industry directorate, offering scaling technology-led businesses managerial training, venture funding and cross-border expansion support within the continental free trade area; no prize fund, entry deadline, cohort size or outcome from the first edition is published

subject: finance.new
name: Pooled equity investment in a pan-African start-up fund
position_end: EUR10.5m approved toward first close - EUR7m from the continental development bank and EUR3.5m from the European Union with the African, Caribbean and Pacific states - into a fund investing in agribusiness, financial services, energy, education and health, mainly in Francophone West Africa

subject: gov.regional
name: West African Backbone Managers Network (ROA-BN)
position_end: Operating, with its headquarters inaugurated at Kagbelen in Conakry on 10 November 2025 and the backbone managers of eight countries as members - Guinea, Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire, Mali, Niger, Sierra Leone, Senegal and Ghana. Its stated mission is interconnection, the pooling of infrastructure and the harmonisation of digital policy between members; its president says the member countries are already interconnected and that the work now is redundancy, naming Mali's links to Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea and Senegal, alongside training for member operators' staff and the sale of transit capacity between them

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime statutes in the Sahel states
position_end: A press-freedom organisation reports the cybercrime statutes of Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Guinea being used to prosecute journalists, and calls for the repeal of vague public-order and human-dignity provisions

subject: gov.legislate
name: ECOWAS Supplementary Act A/SA.2/01/10 on Electronic Transactions
position_end: The community's own act on electronic transactions, adopted alongside the companion act on personal-data protection this ledger holds separately; the full text is now held

subject: gov.protect
name: Seminar of African data-protection authorities
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: Senegal's personal data protection commission opened a sharing seminar in Dakar on Monday 7 September 2026, running to 10 September, bringing together several African and international data-protection authorities to strengthen cooperation between countries, share experience and promote responsible data governance against the demands of digital transformation and artificial intelligence.

subject: dpi.mis
name: ASRII Digital Platform
position_end: Twenty core participants trained across the Commission's directorates with the Directorate of Research and Statistics named as single focal point; the platform is to replace manual collection with submission, validation, automated computation of integration scores and dissemination, and is to be used to evaluate member states' policy implementation and track commitments across sectors. No integration score has been published (2026-08)

subject: dpi.pay
name: BCEAO accession to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System
position_end: A six-month pilot with more than 80 commercial banks is planned before any decision, to test conformity with the union's external-financial-relations rules

subject: dpi.pay
name: BCEAO Instruction 001-03-2021 on oversight of payment infrastructures
position_end: Defines the central bank's governance and oversight role over financial market infrastructures, payment instruments and payment-service providers across the eight member states: classification of systemically important infrastructures, risk-based surveillance principles, reporting obligations, and the corrective measures and sanctions the bank may impose

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Central bank supervisory position on bank cyber-risk
position_start: Not previously held by this base
position_end: The regional central bank's Monetary Policy Committee, meeting in Dakar on 9 September 2026, found the union's banking sector fundamentals sound - bank liquidity near FCFA 7,000 billion, credit to the economy growing and a solvency ratio above the regulatory norm - while calling on banks to remain vigilant against cyberattacks.

subject: infra.store
name: Data-centre capacity gap
position_end: About 150MW to 200MW of new capacity — 30 or more large-scale facilities — needed to reach the capacity-to-population ratio of a moderately mature market such as Morocco, on a regional depth of 0.04MW per million people; as at early 2025 the region was the only one on the continent with no established or announced public cloud region from any of the world's five largest cloud providers

subject: data.statistics
name: ECOMAC (ECOWAS Multilateral Surveillance Mechanism database)
position_end: The database of the bloc's multilateral surveillance mechanism, constituted by a statistical and computer protocol adopted by the Council of Ministers in December 2007: thirteen Excel tables on a quarterly update cadence with stated deadlines, and supervision divided between the monetary union's commission and central bank, the West African Monetary Agency and the West African Monetary Institute; no later amendment and no operational report is held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: ECOWAS Directive C/DIR.1/08/11 on Fighting Cyber Crime
position_end: The community's own cybercrime directive, the instrument the member states' national cybercrime statutes are made against; the full text is held, recovered by optical character recognition from an image-only scan

subject: infra.cybersec
name: ECOWAS Information Sharing and Analysis Centre
position_end: Named by the Commission as established, as the region's threat-intelligence sharing platform; no founding instrument, membership, feed or published output is held (2026-08)

subject: dpi.pay
name: EPSS (ECOWAS Payment and Settlement System)
position_end: Work is on where the platform's components will be hosted and on evaluating the central banks bidding to host them; no build, cost, timetable or legal instrument held

subject: dpi.pay
name: GIM-UEMOA interbank switch
status: Implemented, led on an interim basis
position_end: The regional interbank electronic-payments switch is running under an interim chief executive, its previous director-general having left the post he held from March 2020

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment institutions licensed in the monetary union
position_end: Thirty-one structures licensed as payment institutions across the union under the 2024 payment-services instruction, eleven of them in Senegal and nine in Cote d'Ivoire

subject: dpi.pay
name: UEMOA Regulation 15/2002/CM on payment systems
position_end: The founding regional act for payment systems across the monetary union: it sets the legal basis for electronic signatures and certification, makes bank account access mandatory, promotes scriptural payment instruments, and governs netting, settlement finality and the cheque regime - the frame under which the union's later instant-payment and electronic-money instruments sit

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union electronic money and large-microfinance position
position_end: Union-wide electronic-money outstandings rose 35.2 per cent to CFAF 1,923.2 billion at 31 December 2025 and electronic-money accounts reached 172.9 million, of which only 60.6 million, 35.1 per cent, were active. Senegal held 29.7 per cent of outstandings and 26.5 per cent of large-microfinance assets, leading on both, with CFAF 1,234.3 billion of microfinance assets ahead of Cote d'Ivoire's CFAF 1,226.7 billion and Burkina Faso's CFAF 889.4 billion, the three together holding 71.9 per cent of the union's large-institution assets; Senegal hosts 81 large institutions against Burkina Faso's 50, Togo's 47 and Cote d'Ivoire's 43

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union instruction on payment services
position_end: The union-wide regulatory instrument for payment services, made under the monetary union treaty and the uniform banking, microfinance and anti-money-laundering laws, governing payment services including electronic-money institutions and mobile payment services

subject: infra.connect
name: WACS cable repair logistics
status: Implemented, depot far from the outage zone
position_end: The cable's spare-fibre depot sits at Brest, far from the stretch between Senegal and Congo where most outages occur, so a repair ship had to sail from Portland to Abidjan
